summary.text: Patrick Belmont is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah House of Representatives District 3 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he faces Republican incumbent Jason Thompson.
A professor at Utah State University, he said in a Ballotpedia survey that he is running as an independent focused on accountability and evidence-based decisions.

paragraphs.text: Patrick Belmont was born in Chicago, Illinois, and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Christian University in 2000 and a graduate degree and Ph.D. from Lehigh University in 2007.
His career experience includes working as a professor, and he has served as vice-chair of the Logan City Renewable Energy and Sustainability Advisory Board.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a scientist, educator and longtime Cache Valley resident who teaches at Utah State University.
Belmont ran for District 3 in 2022, when he was listed as a Democrat and incumbent Dan Johnson defeated him 56.6 percent to 43.4 percent.
He ran again in 2024 as an unaffiliated candidate for the open seat, losing to Jason Thompson 54.0 percent to 46.0 percent.
In the survey, Belmont said he is running as an independent because he believes the parties are better at dividing people than bringing them together.
He said he would answer to evidence, conscience and the people he represents rather than party leadership.
